practice_model.philosophy: Practical working-artist education: create consistently, identify a calling and niche early, build a market-ready portfolio, learn to explain and price the work, and develop a sustainable art career.

tuesday.focus: Critique · Portfolio · Artist Writing · External Feedback Planning
tuesday.evidence: critique notes, artist statement drafts, portfolio edits

wednesday.evidence: new work, technical problem solving, experimentation

thursday.focus: Art Business · Marketing · Audience Research · Public Feedback
thursday.rule: turn art into a sustainable practice
thursday.evidence: pricing, market research, outreach, contracts/invoices, marketing assets

friday.focus: Studio Production III · Finish · Photograph · Archive
friday.evidence: finished work, photography/scans, metadata, inventory record

practice_model.studio_rule: At least 60% of scheduled Arts concentration days must produce or materially advance original creative work.
practice_model.portfolio_rule: Every completed work considered for the portfolio must be professionally documented, titled/identified, dated, measured where relevant, and entered into the learner inventory.
practice_model.business_rule: Business learning is applied to the learner's own developing practice: website, online portfolio, business identity, pricing, opportunities, applications, selling systems and reinvestment are built as real artifacts.

borrowed_best_practices.drawing_and_observation: Retain rigorous drawing/seeing as a lifelong artist tool, not as an academic gatekeeping exercise.
borrowed_best_practices.design_2d: Teach composition, color, imaging and visual communication because working artists must control how work reads.
borrowed_best_practices.space_3d: Require material, object, installation and spatial experimentation so students understand form beyond a flat surface.
borrowed_best_practices.time_4d: Expose every student to sequence, sound, motion, performance and video so they can discover whether time-based practice belongs in their niche.
borrowed_best_practices.research: Use artist research, museums, galleries, archives and living practitioners to strengthen original work, not to replace making.
borrowed_best_practices.critique: Teach critique as a professional revision skill: describe, interpret, question, test intention, revise.
borrowed_best_practices.visual_culture: Place the learner's work in historical, cultural and contemporary context without imposing a single canon.
borrowed_best_practices.collaboration: Require at least one collaborative/community experiment to develop communication and shared-production skills.
borrowed_best_practices.sustainability: Include material safety, waste, reuse and responsible production as practical studio decisions.
borrowed_best_practices.audience_and_exhibition: Teach that work is not fully professional until it can be documented, placed, presented and encountered by an audience.

real_world_feedback.philosophy: Feedback should come primarily from real audiences, peers, artists, clients, viewers and public-facing experiments rather than from an internal Khaemenes taste authority.
real_world_feedback.principle: The program teaches learners how to seek, structure, interpret and document feedback; it does not decide whether an artwork is artistically 'correct.'
approved_channels: social media posts or stories with a specific feedback question
self-hosted artist critique circles or studio meetings
local art groups, clubs or maker communities
public libraries, community centers or cultural organizations
pop-up displays, open studios or informal exhibitions
art fairs, markets, festivals or community events
portfolio reviews with practicing artists or creative professionals
online art communities or moderated forums
friends/family only when the feedback question is structured and role bias is acknowledged
artist swaps: exchange critique with another practicing artist
feedback_questions: What do you think this work is communicating?
Where does your attention drop or become confused?
What feels strongest or most memorable?
What feels unfinished, inconsistent or unclear?
Would you want to see more work in this direction? Why or why not?
Where could you imagine encountering or buying/displaying this work?
What words would you use to describe the style or mood?
Which of several works feels most cohesive with the rest of the series?
What questions does the work leave you with?
guardrails: Do not equate likes, follower counts or virality with artistic quality.
Do not require students to reveal private identity, exact location or other sensitive information.
Students may use pseudonyms, controlled audiences or offline events.
Record the source/context of feedback so comments can be interpreted rather than treated as universal truth.
Separate taste feedback from clarity, craft, audience-fit and market feedback.
Do not revise every time someone dislikes a work.
Look for patterns across multiple responses before changing direction.
Treat harassment, abuse and bad-faith comments as noise, not critique.
For minors, public posting must follow parent/guardian and Academy safety rules.
evidence: which feedback was rejected and why
real_world_feedback.outcome: Learners finish Year 1 able to create a repeatable audience-feedback loop that supports artistic development, niche discovery and marketing research.

practice_model.critique_authority: Khaemenes teaches critique frameworks and evidence review but does not act as the final artistic taste authority. Major artistic feedback should be gathered from real audiences, peers, practicing artists, public events and market-facing experiments.

artist_entrepreneurship.name: Artpreneurship Foundations
artist_entrepreneurship.philosophy: Students build a real, low-cost artist business infrastructure while they are still developing their art. Every major business lesson produces a usable artifact.
year1_required_assets: simple artist website built through the Khaemenes course
online portfolio with professional artwork images and metadata
artist bio and short/long artist statements
business card design plus vendor/order comparison and print-ready file
artist opportunity tracker for calls, exhibits, markets and vending events
at least one completed artist-call or exhibit application practice packet
at least one real local opportunity researched
at least one public-facing feedback or market test

website_standard.principle: Teach a simple owned web presence rather than making students dependent on a social platform.

business_card_standard.activity: Compare at least three printing options or local printers, prepare a print-ready card, calculate unit cost, and make an informed order decision. Purchasing is optional; no vendor is required by Khaemenes.

opportunity_finding.rule: Students learn to distinguish legitimate opportunities from pay-to-play or scammy listings.

selling_practice.boundary: Educational only. Students must verify current local/state tax, permit, insurance and vendor rules for the event/location they actually use.

reinvestment_model.name: Artpreneurship Growth Fund
reinvestment_model.purpose: Teach students to treat some art income as future production and business capacity rather than immediately spending all revenue.
reinvestment_model.exercise: Create three reinvestment scenarios based on low, medium and strong sales months; percentages are learner-selected and scenario-based, not prescribed financial advice.
